items.docket_item: sec4:hermes_cli/kanban_db.py kanban_retired() decides retirement through _tombstoned_shape (os.lstat, never following the final symlink): only an absent path or an ordinary regular file reads as not-retired, so a dangling symlink, a symlink to a directory, a fifo or an unreadable path all fail CLOSED
items.notes: P7 part 7 / criterion 8. Path.is_dir() swallows OSError, so the documented fail-closed branch was dead for exactly the three cases it named; a dangling symlink at the canonical path let init_db() create a 118,784-byte board DB through the tombstone.

items.docket_item: sec4:hermes_cli/kanban_db.py six entry points that sit ABOVE or BESIDE the connect() opener gate refuse on the canonical tombstone as their FIRST statement — dispatch_once(conn) and create_task(conn) (take an already-open connection), run_daemon() (hermes kanban daemon, before its first tick), set_current_board() (writes <root>/kanban/current with no DB open), remove_board() (archive/delete of a board directory) and count_notify_subs() (raw read-only sqlite3 open that still mints -wal/-shm sidecars) — plus the write_txn(conn) transaction chokepoint every conn-taking mutator (archive_task, delete_task, add_comment, assign_task, block_task, …) funnels through, and the two DB-less filesystem writers store_attachment_bytes() and resolve_workspace(): a connection opened BEFORE the tombstone was laid, or a path that never calls connect(), can no longer write, delete, archive or dispatch against read-only history (C9/C16/C18)
items.notes: Part 8 patch A (C9/C16/C18). connect() was the only tombstone gate, so anything holding a pre-tombstone connection (long-lived gateway/daemon/worker) or writing without a DB open (current-board pointer, board archive/delete, attachment blobs, workspaces, WAL sidecars from a read-only open) still mutated read-only history. Every guard is the function's first statement, ahead of _assert_not_delegated_child_mutation() and any use of conn; write_txn is the chokepoint for the ~50 conn-taking mutators (fix-pass finding F1). Each proof asserts the KanbanRetiredError AND a byte-identical tree / unchanged row counts.
